claims.location: source name, assay name, comment[data file], comment[fraction identifier], comment[technical replicate] rows 1-912
claims.value: source = MaxQuant experiment name (L1_H1_A1..L14_WT3_2; Corr02A_p42_2018_24, Corr02B_p42_2019_2, Corr4_2018_13, Corr4_2018_11); heavy source = 'super-SILAC standard spiked into <experiment>'; fraction = trailing number of the run name; technical replicate 1 = R1 / untagged series, 2 = R2 series
claims.evidence: summary.txt 'Experiment' column assigns all 456 deposited .raw files: 14 experiments x 24 runs in mqA (R1 and R2 series x 12 fractions) and 4 Corr experiments x 30 runs in mqB/mqC (untagged and R2 series x 15 fractions). Every deposited raw is claimed exactly once (asserted in scripts/make_tables.py). R1/R2 are two complete fraction series of the same experiment; they are encoded as technical replicates 1/2 (inference from run names: the series share experiment, sample and fraction numbers).

claims.value: SILAC light = individual iPSC-CM sample (study sample); SILAC heavy = spike-in super-SILAC standard (reference)
claims.evidence: PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol: heavy 13C6,15N2-Lys / 13C6,15N4-Arg labelled iPSC-CM cultures of the 4 patient-derived and 3 WT lines were pooled at equal protein as the spike-in super-SILAC standard; non-labelled (light) samples from two differentiations of each line were mixed 1:1 with the standard. summary.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 Arg10;Lys8 in all 3 searches. Data check (ratios.txt): log2 H/L normalized of RAS GTPases is lower in H samples (MRAS -0.84..+0.05, HRAS -0.38..+0.11, NRAS -0.42..+0.19, KRAS -0.33..+0.19) than in WT samples (MRAS +1.24/+1.68, HRAS +0.67..+1.33, NRAS +0.37..+0.85, KRAS +0.45..+0.91), with Corr samples intermediate/WT-like (MRAS +0.45..+1.56): RAS accumulation in LZTR1-deficient cells (abstract; follow-up paper western blots) sits in the light channel, so light = individual sample.

claims.location: characteristics[genotype], factor value[genotype], characteristics[disease] rows 1-384 (light rows (first and third 12-row block of each 48-row sample block in rows 1-672; first and third 15-row block of each 60-row block in rows 673-912))
claims.evidence: MaxQuant experiments L1-L8 are H1_A1..H2_B2: 4 lines (H1-A, H1-B, H2-A, H2-B) x 2 differentiations = PRIDE's '4 patient-derived' iPSC lines with 'two individual differentiations of each iPSC line'. The follow-up paper (PMC10851011) states the two affected brothers of Hanses et al. carry biallelic LZTR1 variants c.27dupG (maternal) and c.1943-256C>T (paternal, intron 16). PRIDE projectDescription: 'two siblings displaying an autosomal recessive form of NS ... caused by biallelic mutations within LZTR1'. MONDO:0011531 'Noonan syndrome 2' (xref OMIM:605275, the autosomal-recessive LZTR1 entity) is used, not MONDO:0014693 'Noonan syndrome 10' (OMIM:616564, autosomal dominant), per independent review. RAS accumulation in these samples (ratios) is consistent.

claims.value: LZTR1 intron 16 CRISPR-repaired (patient-derived isogenic); Noonan syndrome 2
claims.evidence: Experiments Corr02A/Corr02B/Corr4_2018_13/Corr4_2018_11 (2019 runs); PRIDE title 'Intronic CRISPR repair in LZTR1-deficient iPSC-cardiomyocytes from Noonan syndrome patients' and dataProcessingProtocol comparison 'NS-corr versus NS'. Follow-up paper: corrected lines are allele-specific edits of the intron 16 variant in the patients' iPSCs. Disease = the donor's disease (MONDO:0011531, autosomal-recessive LZTR1 NS; the corrected lines are edited iPSCs of the affected brothers, not of healthy donors); the repair is captured in genotype/factor value, so the compared variable stays distinct from disease. Normalised RAS ratios (ratios.txt) consistent with repair.

claims.value: light: NS 1-8 (L1..L8), WT 1-6 (L9..L14), corrected 1-4; heavy: pooled
claims.evidence: Each MaxQuant experiment is one independent differentiation (PRIDE: 'Two individual differentiations of each iPSC line'), numbered uniquely within its genotype group (batch rule 3). The standard is a pool.

INFERENCE from experiment names: the 4 patient lines are named H1_A, H1_B, H2_A, H2_B, read as patient (H1/H2) x clone (A/B); PRIDE/follow-up: two affected siblings. H1/H2 are the depositors' labels; mapping to Cellosaurus donors is unknown. The H*-B lines are patient lines (not relatives): PRIDE states '4 patient-derived' lines in the standard and only 3 WT lines, and RAS ratios of H1_B1/H1_B2/H2_B1 are NS-like (log2 H/L MRAS -0.84, HRAS -0.21/+0.11, NRAS -0.42/-0.13/+0.19 vs WT MRAS +1.24/+1.68, HRAS +0.67..+1.33, NRAS +0.37..+0.85).
Follow-up paper: 'We recently identified two brothers ... autosomal recessive NS' (the patients of Hanses et al.); the corrected lines are edited patient iPSCs.

limitations: Primary paper (Circulation 2020, PMID 32623905) and its supplement could not be read: not in PMC, ahajournals 403, Goettingen repository green copy 403 (bot check, not bypassed). Sample identities therefore rest on the PRIDE protocol, the MaxQuant experiment names and the 2024 follow-up paper.

characteristics[cellosaurus accession] / [cellosaurus name] = not available: the follow-up paper names the patient lines UMGi030-A (isHOCMx1.14) and UMGi031-A (isHOCMx2.8) and corrected clones UMGi030-A-1 / UMGi031-A-1, but the deposit's labels (H1-A, H1-B, H2-A, H2-B, Corr02, Corr4, WT1-3) cannot be mapped to them (2 clones per patient in this study, and the WT lines are not named).

Corr02A vs Corr02B: encoded as two differentiations of one corrected line 'Corr02' (both p42, differentiation IDs 2018_24 / 2019_2, parallel to Corr4_2018_13 / _11); they could instead be two clones. Which patient each corrected line derives from is not stated.

Super-SILAC standard of the 2019 corrected-line heavy rows (rows 673-912) is ASSUMED to be the same 4 NS + 3 WT standard as in 2017: the PRIDE protocol describes only one standard and the 'NS-corr versus NS' ratio comparison (dataProcessingProtocol) implies a common reference, but no 2019-specific statement exists.

The follow-up paper (PMC10851011) lists four 'patient-specific' lines including UMGi032-A (NS-R1) and UMGi033-A (NS-R2); Cellosaurus CVCL_A4KP / CVCL_A4KQ record them as a 38Y male and a 28Y female with no disease, i.e. likely the parents/relatives (the follow-up's Figure S6 mentions iPSC-CMs 'from both parents'). They are not assumed to be among H1-A..H2-B: in this deposit the 4 patient-derived lines are read as 2 clones of each of the 2 brothers (experiment names H1_A/H1_B/H2_A/H2_B), supported by NS-like RAS ratios of all H lines incl. H*-B.

R1/R2 run series encoded as technical replicates 1/2 (repeat LC-MS series of the same fractionated sample) from run names only; fractionation method not described in any retrieved source (comment[fractionation method] = not available).

Disease term: MONDO:0011531 'Noonan syndrome 2' replaced MONDO:0014693 'Noonan syndrome 10' after independent review (autosomal-recessive vs autosomal-dominant LZTR1 entity). Age, ancestry and passage number not available at sample level; WT donor sex not available.
